I checked each claim in the document against the record. All of them are supported, so I'm submitting no flags.

- **"Every lookup was refused"** is the closest call. The record's log line (Gd3f7) counts as few as 59 refused lookups out of 200 in one minute, but 200 out of 200 is typical. The low minute is most likely the minute of the deploy at 01:36:39. I read the claim as supported, and it is the one a stricter reader might question.
- **The only went_wrong item ("nobody was paged")** is a finding the record states for itself. It isn't something that field excludes.
- **Action items, figures written in from the record, and what-if sentences** weren't judged, as instructed.

supported.quote: The deployment configuration's summary cache port was changed from {D1.1} to {D1.2}.
Nothing on the cache host accepted connections on the new port, so every cache lookup was refused.
The account page handles an unreachable cache by working each shopper's spend figure out again from scratch, so pages stayed correct but became slow.

A configuration change pointed the shop's account pages at an address where their cache could not be reached, so every page had to work its figures out from scratch, which kept the pages correct but made them slow.
The repository still sets the cache port that refused every lookup, so syncing the repository back into production before a fix is merged could slow account pages again.
The typical (median) time io-shop took to answer a request rose well above its usual level and stayed there, while no more requests failed than usual.
Account pages could not use the rendered-summary cache. Every lookup to it was refused, so the page fell back to working each shopper's spend figure out again on each request, which is the slow path.
Deploy P2 at {P2.1} changed the cache port in deploy/values-production.yaml from {D1.1} to {D1.2} and changed nothing else. As of {T11.1}, all {T11.2} replicas were running that revision.
rows: A file [D1] does not list is as it was

supported.quote: The earlier deploy P1 of revision 544cef3: metrics read back over the hours before the onset show the service healthy with it in place until the onset, and rolling back to it put the service back to normal.
A change to io-shop's source code: the deploy's diff changes only deploy/values-production.yaml.
The change broke the service because nothing accepted connections on the new port, while the old port had served account pages normally.
No check was seen, in review or before the deploy, that the cache address in the deployment configuration accepts connections in production.
No check was seen during the rollout that new replicas could reach the summary cache, so all replicas moved to the revision that could not reach it.
No alert on refused summary cache lookups was seen. The fault was found only by the latency alert, whose rule waits with its condition holding before it fires.
The refused lookups, logged from the minute of the deploy, could have raised an alert sooner, and the rollback would have come sooner.
Nobody was paged: the alert was linked to no on-call incident, so no person was brought in while production was slow.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
